chapter_title: The Long Night Singing Its Dirges
title: Song of Praises
subtitle: People praise the fragrance, the crimson liquid, and everything under its protection.

items.text: Song of Praises
Outside, Tavern
The rowdy sounds from the tavern spilled out into the air.
But the ruckus outside the door wasn't just drunken banter.
Pfft—

items.speaker: George
items.text: Curse you! How much water did you sneak into this drink?!

items.speaker: Tavern Owner
items.text: Get lost, you babbling broke fool!
The drunkard, licking his lips as he slyly pulled out the cork, was more than pleased.

items.speaker: Tavern Owner
items.text: Quit causing a scene.

items.speaker: Tavern Owner
items.text: I can feel those pitiful coins tumbling in your pocket; though they don't amount to much.

items.speaker: George
items.text: Gi... Give me another... I can pay!
Leaning casually against the dirty wall in her pristine robes, someone chimed in.

items.speaker: Dikke
items.text: Two glasses of your best white.
The innkeeper slyly masked his surprise and briskly swung the tavern door open, inviting the magistrate in.

items.speaker: Tavern Owner
items.text: Need anything else? It's snug, sure, but we've got everything you could want!

items.speaker: Tavern Owner
items.text: And, of course, we offer services off the menu!
His suggestive wink went unnoticed; the speaker had no plans to step inside.

items.speaker: Dikke
items.text: I'm looking for someone.

items.speaker: Dikke
items.text: Someone who knows their way around here.
A scruffy man stepped forward with swaggering confidence.

items.speaker: George
items.text: Me name's George, I'm the man you're after!

items.speaker: George
items.text: Want the juicy details about noble affairs, or are you after some excitement?

items.speaker: George
items.text: Trust me, my rates are fair...
He thumped his chest with genuine conviction.

items.speaker: Dikke
items.text: Here, these are for you.

items.speaker: George
items.text: Oh Lord, praise be to your name!

items.speaker: George
items.text: To be trusted by a person of your stature; I vow you have made a wise choice!
Taking a deep breath of the lingering scent of wine, he turned his head away from the innkeeper.

items.speaker: George
items.text: Care for it well! And remember, not a drop of water — I'm won't be so easily fooled!

items.speaker: Tavern Owner
items.text: Tsk.
The figures moved through the streets and alleys.

items.speaker: Dikke
items.text: Is this the market?

items.speaker: George
items.text: Yes, Your Honor.

items.speaker: George
items.text: Merchants from other towns come here to buy and sell their wares. If you're willing to spend a bit, you can find all sorts of treasures.

items.speaker: George
items.text: As for that tall structure there... well, before it was abandoned, it was our tower.
He lowered his voice and leaned in.

items.speaker: George
items.text: Since the great plague, no one has taken care of it... Everyone says there are ghouls inside...

items.speaker: George
items.text: My Lady, I advise you to stay away from there.
Dikke looked around. The few people that passed by avoided eye contact, their faces marked by strange expressions.
She traced the path of their gaze over to a mound nestled in an alley beneath the tower and a solitary cross peeking out from the shadows.

items.speaker: Dikke
items.text: Hmm...?

items.speaker: Dikke
items.text: It seems this is not a market but a graveyard.
Without waiting for a response, Dikke walked towards the alley.
As she entered under the tower's shadow, the mound became fully visible
Withered wildflowers and tangled hay lie around it, the decaying wooden cross sticking out from above. Ants were crawling in lines over it.

items.speaker: Dikke
items.text: Is this grave one of the market's specialties?

items.speaker: George
items.text: This... it must be new... I haven't seen it here before...

items.speaker: George
items.text: Oh... Recently, there have been rumors about these ghouls. Perhaps...
Suddenly, an approaching man pushed George aside, glaring harshly at him.

items.speaker: Malachi
items.text: Step back, filth! Do you dare taint the robes of our honorable magistrate!
The man wheeled around on his heels, bowing in a respectful gesture.

items.speaker: Malachi
items.text: Ah! Honorable Magistrate, I am Malachi.

items.speaker: Malachi
items.text: You've graced us with your presence, at last. Even now, we are patiently awaiting you at the monastery.

items.speaker: Malachi
items.text: But, why are you out here all alone?

items.speaker: Dikke
items.text: It's a habit of mine.
He nodded, then feigning realization adopted a fearful expression.

items.speaker: Malachi
items.text: This drunkard is a madman. If he said anything foolish to you, I beg you forgive him.
He gave the other man a stern look, and his nose twitched.

items.speaker: Malachi
items.text: Huh? You smell of Languedoc? Where did you steal such good wine?—You've committed a crime, boy!

items.speaker: George
items.text: Pah, I stole nothing!... This was my hard-earned reward.

items.speaker: Malachi
items.text: We'll deal with this later!—Magistrate!
He put on a new smile to accompany his changed face.

items.speaker: Dikke
items.text: I believe you have another matter to discuss.

items.speaker: Dikke
items.text: Unreported deaths, is that right?

items.speaker: Malachi
items.text: No, no, no, My Lady, you misunderstand.

items.speaker: Malachi
items.text: Of course, we were planning to report this to you, but... we needed first to organize the complete records.
The man spoke haltingly.

items.speaker: Dikke
items.text: No matter, I had no intention of combing through your tedious records.

items.speaker: Dikke
items.text: You may state your case in person.

items.speaker: Malachi
items.text: He ...
The sound of an impatient rapping of fingers rose and fell along Lady Dikke's sword, echoing into Malachi's ears.

items.speaker: Dikke
items.text: You have nothing to fear. Please ... continue.

items.speaker: Malachi
items.text: ...The deceased was a monk... Brother Chester.

items.speaker: George
items.text: Ah! It's him...
Malachi shot him another glance.

items.speaker: Dikke
items.text: Go on.

items.speaker: George
items.text: I've heard some rumors; people say he's the one you've hidden away, the one that had turned into a ghoul...

items.speaker: Malachi
items.text: Shut your mouth, or would you like to forfeit your rations?
The man pulled back his neck.

items.speaker: Malachi
items.text: According to our initial investigation, Chester appears to have died due to a drunken misstep...
He nervously scanned the surroundings.

items.speaker: Dikke
items.text: Father Malachi, is there something you'd rather not discuss openly?

items.speaker: Malachi
items.text: Several residents reported witnessing odd behavior from Brother Chester, that he had a peculiar offensive odor about him... some even claim to have seen him sneaking into the tower...

items.speaker: Malachi
items.text: And others say they saw him carrying a corpse through the town at night. Convinced that he was a ghoul.

items.speaker: Dikke
items.text: And is there any truth to these claims?
Malachi's voice dropped.

items.speaker: Malachi
items.text: Of course not, My Lady! Ghouls are nothing more than superstition... Yet, heaven only knows... Perhaps he was a wizard.

items.speaker: Dikke
items.text: Huh...

items.speaker: Malachi
items.text: ...The elders think so too.

items.speaker: Dikke
items.text: So, then you assume his death came from a spell that backfired?
He leaned in, whispering in a voice only the two could hear.

items.speaker: Malachi
items.text: My Lady, it doesn't really matter what the truth is.

items.speaker: Malachi
items.text: Should it be revealed that the monastery concealed a wizard, it wouldn't sit well with the townspeople.
His breath ran thin as he advised the young woman in front of him.

items.speaker: Malachi
items.text: Though the Great Plague is over, the people's trust in us has not yet been restored.

items.speaker: Malachi
items.text: "Can the monastery really protect us? Can they?"—You must have heard such doubts.

items.speaker: Malachi
items.text: Whether a wizard or a ghoul, either one would profane the monastery by their presence.

items.speaker: Malachi
items.text: It leaves us in a precarious position, I'm sure I need not say more.
He nodded in approval, as if he were satisfied by his own words.

items.speaker: Dikke
items.text: You have your reasons.

items.speaker: Malachi
items.text: Hmm...

items.speaker: Dikke
items.text: But I don't accept them.

items.speaker: Malachi
items.text: What...?!
He stared in astonishment at the young magistrate.

items.speaker: Dikke
items.text: As of now, I'm unsure where the truth lies. What I do know is that it won't be discovered in empty words or false advice.

items.speaker: Malachi
items.text: You should know... the affairs of wizards are most elusive, it will be difficult for us to gather substantial evidence.

items.speaker: Dikke
items.text: That, Father ... is precisely my work.
Malachi tried to suppress his anger.

items.speaker: Malachi
items.text: Perhaps you don't quite understand what I'm saying...

items.speaker: Malachi
items.text: The people need the comfort of reassurance, not harsh realities, my Lady.

items.speaker: Malachi
items.text: Please, you should—

items.speaker: Dikke
items.text: What you should do, Father, is provide me useful information.

items.speaker: Dikke
items.text: Not stand in my way and presume to dictate my mission.
"Woosh—!"

items.speaker: Malachi
items.text: Of course, of course...
He nodded fervently.

items.speaker: Dikke
items.text: I thank you for your assistance.
The cold metal blade dropped, as if finally satisfied.
TO BE CONTINUED…
